elements.element: Customer is not subject to any restriction on soliciting Vendor personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 expressly states that nothing in the Agreement restricts Customer from soliciting any person employed by Vendor.

elements.element: A non-solicitation covenant binds Customer and Vendor mutually.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause creates no non-solicitation covenant for either party; it instead expressly preserves Customer's freedom to solicit Vendor employees.

elements.element: Any non-solicitation covenant is limited to personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: No non-solicitation covenant exists, so there is no broader covered population requiring limitation.

elements.element: Any non-solicitation covenant lasts no more than 12 months from the end of each covered person's involvement in the Services.
elements.evidence: No non-solicitation covenant or restriction period exists, so no restriction extends beyond the permitted duration.

elements.element: Any non-solicitation covenant excludes general advertisements and responses to them.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly preserves hiring of persons who respond to general recruitment, and Section 12.4 imposes no solicitation restriction.

elements.element: Any non-solicitation covenant excludes unsolicited approaches by personnel.
elements.evidence: There is no non-solicitation covenant, and Section 12.4 broadly confirms that Customer may engage any person employed by Vendor, which encompasses persons who approach Customer unsolicited.

elements.element: Neither party is prohibited from hiring or engaging the other party's personnel.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 confirms that Customer made no no-hire commitment, Section 12.4 expressly permits Customer to engage Vendor employees, and the rendered language imposes no hiring or engagement prohibition on Vendor.

result.reason: The operative redline fully achieves the preferred position by eliminating Customer's non-solicitation restriction and affirmatively preserving its freedom to solicit. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because it creates no mutual non-solicitation covenant, although all fallback limitations and protections are either expressly present or rendered unnecessary by the absence of such a covenant. The change is confined to removing the original solicitation and engagement restriction and is consistent with Section 12.3's existing no-hire language.
